why.trigger: the v18 re-derivation verification passed all three candidates, but it declares rule_applied as the ORIGINAL rule file and never mentions the amendment, so its three passes were decided against a superseded rule
why.what_that_leaves_open: under the original rule the surviving literals include BLOCK and COMMENT for django-15572 and get_response, inner and request for django-16255; those are exactly the tokens the amendment was written to exclude
why.my_own_over_tightening: the amendment's tightened requirement 1 demanded that EVERY literal appear in the defect-carrying view, which would reject django-15569 for its third literal even though that constant is genuinely part of the same machinery; that formulation was too strict and is corrected here
why.no_candidate_may_be_registered_on_a_supe: registering now would silently lower the evidence bar of the only task set that can carry a citable number

literal_requirements: R1 every required literal appears verbatim in at least one registered view, with its source view recorded

R2 at least two of the at most three literals are code anchored: a name the views bind (function, class, method, assignment target or parameter), a constant token such as E015 or 3.8.3 or a type name such as NoneType, or a quoted string constant that is not in the declared common word list
R3 both tokens of the frozen regex, the cause token and the fix token, are code anchored
R4 every literal is relevant to the defect: it is either named by the problem statement or bound inside the defect-carrying view, namely the view whose symbol the statement names
R5 at least two of the literals are absent from the declared framework generic list: request, response, get_response, view, model, field, template, inner, value, error, object, class, method
R6 no literal is a Python keyword or a builtins name

R7 the lazy answer negative control fails: a line assembled from the issue identifier, the statement's own tokens, Python generic vocabulary and the framework generic list must not satisfy the frozen regex or the literal requirement
corrected_rule.what_changed_against_the_previous_amendm: R4 replaces the requirement that every literal sit in the defect-carrying view: relevance may come from the statement naming it, and the defect view requirement now applies as a disjunction rather than to every literal; R5 keeps the framework generic exclusion at two of three literals

calibration.v16_sealed_literals: _check_ordering, E015, __pk; get_context, checked, SplitArrayField; _cull, NoneType, cull_num - all pass R1 to R7 against their own statements and views

v18_current_sets_under_this_rule.django-15572 template_changed, BLOCK, CO: fails R4 for BLOCK and COMMENT: neither is named by the statement nor bound in the defect-carrying view
v18_current_sets_under_this_rule.django-16255 get_response, inner, reques: fails R5: all three are on the framework generic list
v18_current_sets_under_this_rule.django-15569 RegisterLookupMixin, _unreg: RegisterLookupMixin and _unregister_lookup pass R1 to R7; LOOKUP_SEP fails R4 unless the statement names it, so it must be replaced by a name bound in the defect-carrying view

corrected_rule.consequence: the three candidate literal sets must be re-derived once more under this corrected rule; views, ranges, tool names and view hashes stay exactly as they are; a candidate that cannot produce a compliant set is rejected and is never replaced by a weaker one

registration_gate: the source registration must record, per candidate, which rule file and which amendments were applied, and must not be written while any candidate's set fails R1 to R7; the verification artifact must cite the rule file and both amendments by path and hash
